summary: A 30-foot wooden tower on Signal Hill near Custer, manned only in emergencies in 1939; now gone, and listed as a former tower site.

facts.status_note: The tower is gone; a 2020 guide lists the site as a former tower site.

events.note: A 30-foot wooden tower is described in July 1939; the build date is not given.
Manned only in emergencies, per the July 1939 Rapid City Journal item.
SDPB's guide to Black Hills towers lists Signal Hill among former tower sites with no extant tower.

evidence.supports: 30-foot wooden tower, July 1939, about three miles NW of Alkali Springs
evidence.quote: There is a 30-foot wooden tower at Signal hill located in the Limestone country about three miles northwest of Alkali springs.

evidence.supports: manned only in emergencies; area surveyed from Elk Mountain and Summit Ridge
evidence.quote: This station is manned only during times of emergencies, as the area covered by this lookout is now adequately surveyed by Elk mountain and Summit ridge stations.

evidence.supports: placed in Black Hills National Forest
former tower site, no extant tower
evidence.quote: Former tower sites — Boulder Hill, Castle Peak, Cicero Peak, Crows Nest Peak, Flag Mountain, Norris Peak, Parker Peak, Pilger Mountain, Signal Hill, Terry Peak, Veterans Peak — are not.

sources.title: Your Comprehensive List of (South Dakota) Black Hills Lookout Towers

notes_for_editor: Gone status is supported by three sources (firelookout.com, the FFLA list, and SDPB's 2020 guide, which lists it as a former site). The 1939 description is the only account of the tower itself and comes via Forest Lookouts, which quotes the Rapid City Journal; the newspaper was not read. The brief's height_m 9.1 equals 30 feet, but the 1939 text does not say whether that is to the cab floor, so height_m was not written to facts. Brief's coordinates differ from the firelookout.com sources key by roughly 70 m; no correction proposed. No source gives a date for removal or describes the hilltop now, and no access information was found; access was left out.
